extracted.intended_audience: researchers and peer reviewers (including early-career researchers) and journal editors interested in reviewer recognition
extracted.subtask_description: Explaining how the Publons platform documents, verifies, and recognizes peer-review activity so reviewers can receive credit and visibility for their work. Includes privacy/consent rules, publisher integrations, and recognition programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of verified peer reviews and editorial records for career purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers who sign up to Publons can use their verified peer reviews and editorial records for funding and promotion applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publons lets researchers track and showcase peer review activity across journals; verified records can be cited in promotion and funding dossiers as evidence of scholarly service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve reviewer anonymity by default
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the service does not affect reviewer anonymity. By default, the content of the reports is not publicly displayed and only the year of the review and the name of the journal appear on a reviewer’s profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publons maintains confidentiality unless explicit consent is given; profile entries show only minimal metadata (year and journal) unless the reviewer and journal agree to reveal the report content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent-based openness of review reports after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the report can be made open access after a paper has been published only if both the reviewer and the journal agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review text is not automatically public — making reviews open requires joint consent from reviewer and journal, balancing transparency with confidentiality and journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with publishers and ORCID to authenticate and connect reviewer activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Publons has partnerships with several leading scientific publishers and works with ORCID so scientists can easily connect their reviewer activities to their ORCID record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established publisher integrations (BMJ, SAGE, Cambridge University Press, Springer Nature, IOP Publishing, Wiley, etc.) and ORCID linkage enable automatic verification and smoother inclusion of review records in researcher profiles and workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition programs and awards for outstanding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Publons rewards top referees several times per year and introduced initiatives such as the Sentinels of Science Awards to honor 'the highest achievers in peer review across the world’s journals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal awards and partnered programs are part of the recognition ecosystem; participation and performance (as tracked/verified by Publons and publishers) can qualify reviewers for prizes and public acknowledgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition as a lever to increase reviewer engagement and speed
rubrics_metrics.description: A Wiley pilot integrating journals with Publons showed an improvement in reviewer acceptance rates for the pilot journals—and faster review times among the reviewers that opted in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence from publisher pilots suggests that acknowledging reviewers (through verified records/recognition) can improve acceptance of review invitations and reduce turnaround times; this is a practical objective when designing recognition systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal feedback and acknowledgement as valued rewards
rubrics_metrics.description: A survey carried out in 2015 showed that most participants said that feedback from the journals they review for and acknowledgment are the best rewards for these efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design recognition mechanisms to include meaningful feedback and explicit acknowledgment from journals, since reviewers value these forms of reward highly.
